# SB-1027: Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

Hazard description
- Overview: A quench oil fire hazard has been identified associated with improper ventilation and dust accumulation in the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02). The immediate ignition source in recorded events was a hot work spark interacting with oil-saturated dust and deposits in ductwork and collector housings. Contributing factors include reduced dust collector performance, inadequate changeout of accumulated particulate, and flows that allow oil-laden dust to accumulate at high-energy impingement points.
- Key indicator: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa. Persistent or frequent activation of this alarm indicates filter loading, reduced airflow, and increased likelihood of particulate settling and oil retention within the system.
- Background: In operations where ferrous grinding and shot blasting are followed by quenching in oil, airborne particulates can become oil-coated. When the ventilation system does not maintain designed airflow, these particulates are more likely to deposit inside the collector, ductwork, and transition pieces. If ignition occurs in a deposit-rich zone, fire propagation to the quench tank and surrounding oil-handling equipment is possible.
- Risk outcomes: Fire involving quench oil presents rapid flame spread, potential vapour flash, and thermal exposure to adjacent hot forging equipment. Secondary risks include loss of quench media, extended production downtime, and exposure of personnel to smoke and thermal hazards.

Affected equipment
- Primary: Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02).
- Associated systems: Dust collector and ductwork serving EQ-P3-L1-SB02; local quench oil storage and transfer lines that interface with the quench tank; electrical junctions and hot work zones adjacent to the collector and ductwork.
- Plant context: This bulletin applies to operations on line P3-L1 within Plant P3 where EQ-P3-L1-SB02 is used and to maintenance and process personnel who service the dust collector and quench oil systems.

Required controls
- Immediate actions for operation:
  - Monitor the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa. Any alarm condition must be treated as a priority and investigated immediately by operations personnel.
  - Stop all non-essential hot work in the vicinity until the alarm condition is resolved and a clearance is recorded by maintenance.
  - Reduce quench oil flow to non-critical operations where safe to do so and initiate visual inspection of the collector inlet, filters, and duct transitions for oil-wetted deposits.
- Inspection and cleaning controls:
  - Inspect ductwork and collector internals for oil-saturated particulate when the pressure drop alarm indicates compromised airflow. Focus inspection on elbow and transition sections where particle impingement is common.
  - Clean or remove oil-saturated dust deposits before restarting full operations. If deposits are present in difficult-to-access zones, arrange for confined access procedures and fire watch.
- Engineering and administrative controls:
  - Maintain filter change and cleaning activities in accordance with MM-P3-L1-SB02 and the operating sequences in SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-05. These documents contain procedural steps for maintenance and safe operation of the dust collection and quench systems.
  - Ensure hot work permits and fire watches are enforced for work on or near the dust collector, ductwork, and quench oil systems. Hot work must not commence until the collector is verified clean and the local area has been cleared of oil-saturated deposits.
- Fire protection and detection:
  - Confirm fire detection and suppression systems serving the collector and quench area are functional and have current service records. Coordinate with the fire protection team for any changes to system coverage after ductwork or collector modifications.
- Training and awareness:
  - Train operations and maintenance staff on the significance of the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa and the specific steps to take when it activates.
  - Include examples of oil-saturated dust risks in operator toolbox talks and maintenance briefings, using case studies drawn from internal incident summaries and related guidance in MM-P3-L1-SB02.

Step rationale and examples
- Rationale: The alarm threshold noted above reflects degraded airflow and increased particulate loading. When filters and ducts retain oil-laden dust, the potential for smoldering or ignition increases, especially near hot work sources. Removing the combustible load and restoring designed airflow are primary mitigations to break the ignition chain.
- Example scenario: An operator observes the dust collector alarm and documents it. Maintenance inspects and finds oil-wetted deposits in a transition elbow. The deposits are removed under a controlled procedure with a fire watch. Filters are replaced per MM-P3-L1-SB02. Only after confirmation that the pressure drop alarm is no longer active does normal quench operation resume, preventing a possible ignition sequence.

Records to keep
- Maintain an incident log for each activation of the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa. Record the time of activation, operator actions, maintenance findings, cleaning or repairs performed, and clearance to resume operations.
- File maintenance records that reference MM-P3-L1-SB02, and operational checklists completed in accordance with SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-05.
- Keep hot work permits and fire watch logs for any work conducted on collector internals or adjacent ductwork. Retain these records in the equipment maintenance folder for EQ-P3-L1-SB02.

Effective date
- Effective date: Rev E

Related documents
- MM-P3-L1-SB02
- SOP-P3-L1-02
- SOP-P3-L1-05

Distribution: Operations, Maintenance, Safety, and Fire Protection teams for Plant P3, line P3-L1.
